q: The production of new organisms from the existing organisms of the same species is called ____.
e: The production of new organisms from the existing organisms of the same species is called reproduction. Reproduction makes a new generation so the species can continue.

q: A new individual produced from a single parent without involving the sex cell (gamete) is called ____.
e: A new individual produced from a single parent without involving the sex cell (gamete) is called asexual reproduction. Reproduction makes a new generation so the species can continue. Asexual reproduction makes offspring from one parent without gametes fusing.

q: In budding, a small part of a body of the parent organism grows out as a bud which then ____ and becomes a new organism.
e: In budding, a small part of a body of the parent organism grows out as a bud which then detaches and becomes a new organism. Detaches is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The breaking up of the body of a simple multicellular organism into two or more fragments is called ____.
e: The breaking up of the body of a simple multicellular organism into two or more fragments is called fragmentation. Fragmentation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The parent plant produces many microscopic reproductive units called ____ inside the spore sac.
e: The parent plant produces many microscopic reproductive units called spores inside the spore sac. Spores is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In vegetative propagation, new plants are obtained from the parts of old plants such as stems, leaves or roots without the help of any ____ organ.
e: In vegetative propagation, new plants are obtained from the parts of old plants such as stems, leaves or roots without the help of any reproductive organ. Reproductive is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The process of growing many plants from one plant by man-made method is called ____.
e: The process of growing many plants from one plant by man-made method is called artificial method of vegetative propagation. Artificial method of vegetative propagation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A small part of root, stem, or leaves from a plant which is cut with a sharp knife is called ____.
e: A small part of root, stem, or leaves from a plant which is cut with a sharp knife is called cutting. Cutting is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The shoot of the parent plant is allowed to develop roots while it is intact with the plant in a process called ____.
e: The shoot of the parent plant is allowed to develop roots while it is intact with the plant in a process called layering. Layering is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The cut stem having roots is called ____, while the cut stem of another plant without roots is called ____.
e: The cut stem having roots is called stock; scion, while the cut stem of another plant without roots is called. Stock; scion is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The production of new plant from two parent plants by the use of sex cells (gametes) is called ____.
e: The production of new plant from two parent plants by the use of sex cells (gametes) is called sexual reproduction. Sexual reproduction joins gametes from two parents and mixes genes. Reproduction makes a new generation so the species can continue.

q: Fertilization takes place inside the ovary inside which is the ____ gamete.
e: Fertilization takes place inside the ovary inside which is the female gamete. Female is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The body of the ovule is termed as the ____, which is covered by layers of integuments.
e: The body of the ovule is termed as the nucellus, which is covered by layers of integuments. Nucellus is the idea that completes this fact.

q: At the time of pollination, the stigma is viscous with a sticky substance containing sugar and other compounds that stimulates the pollen grains to ____.
e: At the time of pollination, the stigma is viscous with a sticky substance containing sugar and other compounds that stimulates the pollen grains to germinate. Germinate is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The pollen tube penetrates the stigma and grows down the style until it finally reaches the ____.
e: The pollen tube penetrates the stigma and grows down the style until it finally reaches the ovule. Ovule is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The process of fertilization is termed as ____, where the male gametes fuse with the female gamete.
e: The process of fertilization is termed as fertilization, where the male gametes fuse with the female gamete. Fertilization is the joining of male and female gametes.

q: The fusion of three nuclei, i.e., the two polar nuclei and the male gamete, is termed as ____.
e: The fusion of three nuclei, i.e., the two polar nuclei and the male gamete, is termed as triple fusion. Triple fusion is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The ovules develop into seeds and the ovary as a whole changes to form a ____.
e: The ovules develop into seeds and the ovary as a whole changes to form a fruit. Fruit is the idea that completes this fact.

q: During the process of fertilization, the synergids direct the male gamete towards the ____ cell and the polar nuclei.
e: During the process of fertilization, the synergids direct the male gamete towards the egg cell and the polar nuclei. Gametes are sex cells such as sperm and egg.

q: In humans, an ovum from a female is fertilized by a sperm from a male after ____.
e: In humans, an ovum from a female is fertilized by a sperm from a male after sexual intercourse. Sexual intercourse is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The period between fertilization and birth is called ____.
e: The period between fertilization and birth is called gestation period. Gestation period is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The female reproductive organs include the ____, which contains follicles in which ova are produced.
e: The female reproductive organs include the ovary, which contains follicles in which ova are produced. Ovary is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The muscular tube that links the testis to the urethra to allow the passage of semen is called ____.
e: The muscular tube that links the testis to the urethra to allow the passage of semen is called sperm duct. Sperm duct is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The process of cell division that produces the gametes is called ____.
e: The process of cell division that produces the gametes is called meiosis. Meiosis is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The zygote or embryo then grows into a new ____.
e: The zygote or embryo then grows into a new individual. Individual is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In humans, the embryo eventually develops into a ____ with recognizable human features.
e: In humans, the embryo eventually develops into a foetus with recognizable human features. Foetus is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The muscular uterine walls begin to contract during ____, allowing the baby to be born.
e: The muscular uterine walls begin to contract during labour, allowing the baby to be born. Labour is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Lactation is the process of producing ____ in the mother’s breasts for feeding the baby.
e: Lactation is the process of producing milk in the mother’s breasts for feeding the baby. Milk is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The period of bleeding when the dead egg together with the uterus lining is discharged through the vagina is termed ____.
e: The period of bleeding when the dead egg together with the uterus lining is discharged through the vagina is termed menstruation. Menstruation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Inheritance is the transmission of ____ information from generation to generation.
e: Inheritance is the transmission of genetic information from generation to generation. Genetic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The inheritance of certain characteristics such as plant height and skin colour is called ____.
e: The inheritance of certain characteristics such as plant height and skin colour is called heredity. Heredity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The branch of biology that studies how heredity works is called ____.
e: The branch of biology that studies how heredity works is called genetics. Genetics is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chromosome is an organized package of ____ found in the nucleus of the cell.
e: Chromosome is an organized package of DNA found in the nucleus of the cell. The nucleus stores DNA, the cell's genetic instructions. DNA carries the genetic information that cells use to build and run an organism.

q: Each chromosome is made up of DNA and ____.
e: Each chromosome is made up of DNA and proteins. Proteins is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Each chromosome has certain characteristics when it is ready to ____.
e: Each chromosome has certain characteristics when it is ready to divide. Divide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Each chromatid is a string of ____, coding for the person’s characteristics.
e: Each chromatid is a string of genes, coding for the person’s characteristics. Genes is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A human body (somatic) cell nucleus contains ____ pairs of chromosomes.
e: A human body (somatic) cell nucleus contains 23 pairs of chromosomes. 23 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The arrangement of chromosomes in a cell is called a ____.
e: The arrangement of chromosomes in a cell is called a karyotype. Karyotype is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The gene is the basic physical and functional unit of ____.
e: The gene is the basic physical and functional unit of heredity. Heredity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Each gene occupies a specific position on a chromosome called a ____.
e: Each gene occupies a specific position on a chromosome called a locus. Locus is the idea that completes this fact.

q: One of the alternative forms of a gene is called an ____.
e: One of the alternative forms of a gene is called an allele. Allele is the idea that completes this fact.

q: DNA is the chemical substance found in the chromosomes of the ____.
e: DNA is the chemical substance found in the chromosomes of the nucleus. The nucleus stores DNA, the cell's genetic instructions. The nucleus is the control centre of a eukaryotic cell.

q: A molecule of DNA is made from two strands of ____.
e: A molecule of DNA is made from two strands of nucleotides. Nucleotides is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Each nucleotide contains a nitrogenous base which is either adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C), or ____.
e: Each nucleotide contains a nitrogenous base which is either adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C), or guanine (G). Guanine (G) is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In the two strands of DNA, nucleotides with adenine are always paired to opposite nucleotides with ____.
e: In the two strands of DNA, nucleotides with adenine are always paired to opposite nucleotides with thymine. Thymine is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Complementary bases always bind with each other, following the base-pairing rule known as ____.
e: Complementary bases always bind with each other, following the base-pairing rule known as base-pairing. A base reacts with an acid to give a salt and water.

q: DNA can replicate itself, allowing the passing of genetic information from one generation to the ____.
e: DNA can replicate itself, allowing the passing of genetic information from one generation to the next. Next is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Cellular reproduction is a process by which cells duplicate their contents and then ____ to produce two similar cells.
e: Cellular reproduction is a process by which cells duplicate their contents and then divide to produce two similar cells. Divide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Cell division consists of four stages: prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and ____.
e: Cell division consists of four stages: prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase. Telophase is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The two distinct types of cell division are mitosis and ____.
e: The two distinct types of cell division are mitosis and meiosis. Meiosis is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Mitosis is important for regulating cell growth, development, and ____.
e: Mitosis is important for regulating cell growth, development, and repair. Repair is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Meiosis creates genetic variation through sexual reproduction and reduces the chromosome number by ____ of the parent cell.
e: Meiosis creates genetic variation through sexual reproduction and reduces the chromosome number by half of the parent cell. Half is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The inheritance of characteristics in an organism is contributed equally by the ____ and father.
e: The inheritance of characteristics in an organism is contributed equally by the mother and father. Mother is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The dominant trait is expressed in an organism, suppressing the ____ trait.
e: The dominant trait is expressed in an organism, suppressing the recessive trait. Recessive is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The trait that does not get to express itself is called the ____ trait.
e: The trait that does not get to express itself is called the recessive trait. Recessive is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Genetics is the study of heredity and variations of inherited characteristics, and the way that characters are passed on from one ____ to the next.
e: Genetics is the study of heredity and variations of inherited characteristics, and the way that characters are passed on from one generation to the next. Generation is the idea that completes this fact.
